# SharePoint lists of Pursuit Managed Services

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-lists-reference.js from public/js/pms-schema.js and public/js/pms-schema-meta.js. Do not edit by hand: change the schema file and run `npm run build:lists-reference` (scripts/test-lists-reference.js fails when this file is stale). -->

The app keeps everything in 12 SharePoint lists and one picture library on one site. This is the reference to every list and every column: what it is for, who uses it, and exactly how SharePoint must have it. It describes **schema version 3**, the lists of the new site (Phase 10c-2b). The lists of the old site are described in PROVISIONING.md, which is kept as a record.

**Where it comes from.** One file says what every list and column is: `public/js/pms-schema.js` (the names, which every page carries) and `public/js/pms-schema-meta.js` (everything else, which only Setup, the tests and this generator read). The data layer, Setup's Check Lists, the mocked SharePoint of the tests, the local server and the seed checker are all built on it.

**Titles and copies.** Each title below is the list's title when a copy of the app has no prefix (`"listPrefix": ""` in `pms-config.txt`, said on purpose: a page must be told its prefix). A copy with `"listPrefix": "Test"` uses `TestPMSClients` and so on, and `TestPMSClientImages` for the pictures. A single list can also be given a title of its own (`"lists": { "<key>": "<title>" }`), and the library (`"logoLibrary"`). The key of each list (`clients`, `sessions`...) is the code's name for it and never changes.

**The version.** The item `default` of PMSAppSettings carries `SchemaVersion` (3 for these lists). Setup writes it when it makes the lists, and raises an earlier version once the check of this one is clean (Phase 10i); nothing else writes it, and no item is made by hand. Every page reads that item first, so the check costs no request: a missing item, a missing list or no version stops the participant and admin pages with PMS-LST-010, a lower version with PMS-LST-011, a higher one with PMS-LST-012; Setup opens and says which.

**Rules for every list.**

- `AppId` is the app's own id of an item (never SharePoint's numeric ID): single line of text, required, indexed, enforce unique values.
- Every column below must exist on its list, with exactly its internal name and type. No column but AppId is required to hold a value ("Require that this column contains information" is off): many are legitimately empty.
- An index on exactly the columns the app filters on, and on no other column. A query on a column with no index fails once a list passes 5,000 items.
- A column of chosen words is a single line of text, not a Choice: its allowed words are listed below and checked by the app.
- Every date column shows **Date & Time**, never Date Only: a date-only value can be read back as the day before, by the site's time zone (SessionDate included).
- A Yes/No column defaults to No. A single line of text holds 255 characters at most; where the app's own limit is lower it is given.
- Ordered children are JSON lists of ids, kept as plain text of several lines; the app replaces the whole value on every write.
- The built-in Title is filled by the app (the record's title, name or id). Content approval and attachments off unless policy requires them.

## Glossary

The code, the screens and the lists use different words for some lists.

| In the code | On screen | List |
|---|---|---|
| `sections` | activities | PMSActivities |
| `tracks` | participants / visits | PMSParticipants |
| `qrtokens` | guest QR codes | PMSGuestQRCodes |
| `visitorroster` | guest list | PMSGuestList |
| `uservisitlogs` | visit log | PMSVisitLog |
| `responses` | answers | PMSParticipantAnswers |

## The lists

| Key | Title | What it is for | Read by | Written by | Items per event | Items per year (assumed) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clients` | PMSClients | One item for each client: its name, its slug and its look. | participant, admin, setup | admin, setup | 0 or 1 | new clients only (tens) |
| `sessions` | PMSClientSessions | One item for each client and day: the session participants join when it is live. | participant, admin | admin, participant | 1 | 100 |
| `sections` | PMSActivities | The activities: each belongs to one client and holds its questions in order. | participant, admin, setup | admin, setup | 0 (content is per client) | about 2 to 5 per new client, and copies |
| `questions` | PMSActivityQuestions | The questions of every activity. | participant, admin | admin, setup | 0 | about 9 per new client |
| `options` | PMSAnswerOptions | The answers a question offers, including which one is right. | participant, admin | admin, setup | 0 | about 32 per new client |
| `tracks` | PMSParticipants | One item for each visit: one person on one device in one session. | participant, admin | participant, admin | 60 | 6,000 |
| `qrtokens` | PMSGuestQRCodes | One item for each single-use QR code. | participant, admin, setup | admin, participant | up to 60 in guest mode | up to 6,000 |
| `appsettings` | PMSAppSettings | One item, `default`: which session and client are live, and the version of the lists. Every page reads it first. Setup writes it when it makes the lists; nobody makes it by hand. | participant, admin, setup | admin, setup | 0 | 1 in total |
| `visitorroster` | PMSGuestList | The guest list: one item for each named guest of a session. | participant, admin | admin | up to 60 in guest mode | up to 6,000 |
| `uservisitlogs` | PMSVisitLog | The visit log: one row for each browser tab that opened the participant page. Results read it for names. | admin | participant | 60 or more | 6,000 to 9,000 |
| `adminusers` | PMSAdminUsers | The facilitators who may unlock the admin page: a name and a hash of a PIN each. | admin | setup | 0 | a handful in total |
| `responses` | PMSParticipantAnswers | The answers: one item for each visit, holding all of that person's answers. | participant, admin | participant, admin, setup | 60 | 6,000 |

Growth is an ASSUMPTION from ARCHITECTURE-10.md 4.1, in git history at 7347c72 (100 events a year with 60 people each), to be replaced with real figures. Tracks (participants), answers and the visit log pass 5,000 items in under a year at that volume: that is why the indexes matter.

| `AppId` | Single line of text | yes | yes | yes | yes |  | 255 |  | no | The record's own id: the visit's id (a Tracks.AppId), the same as TrackId: one item for each person. | participant, admin | participant, admin, setup |
| `SessionId` | Single line of text | yes | yes | no | no |  | 255 |  | no | The session (a Sessions.AppId): how a session's answers are read together. | participant, admin | participant, admin, setup |
| `ResponsesJson` | Multiple lines of text, plain text (append-only off) | yes | no | no | no |  | 60,000 | [] | **yes** | The person's answers as a JSON list of { questionId, answer, firstAnswer, attempts, correct, answeredAt }. A written answer is 1,000 characters at most and the whole list 60,000. | participant, admin | participant, admin, setup |
| `TrackId` | Single line of text | yes | yes | no | no |  | 255 |  | no | The visit (a Tracks.AppId): how a person's own device finds its answers. | participant, admin | participant, admin, setup |
| `ClientId` | Single line of text | yes | no | no | no |  | 255 |  | no | The client (a Clients.AppId). | participant, admin | participant, admin, setup |

## Columns no longer used

Version 3 (Phase 10i) renamed two columns. SharePoint gives every list item a property called `DisplayName`, and the real site (PCOE, 15 Oct 2026) would not return a column of that name when a read named it ("Value does not fall within the expected range."). A site made for an earlier version keeps its old column: nothing reads or writes it, the check does not look at it, and Setup never deletes it (its plan lists it as harmless); a site owner may delete it by hand. No column of the app may be named like a property SharePoint gives every list item: `scripts/test-schema.js` lists them.

| List | Column | Last used in version | Its value is kept in, since |
|---|---|---|---|
| PMSGuestList | `DisplayName` | 2 | `GuestName` |
| PMSVisitLog | `DisplayName` | 2 | `SignedInName` |

## The picture library: PMSClientImages

A document library (not a folder in Shared Documents). The clients' pictures (hero badge, logo, background, answer tiles), each stored once under a name made from its content. Read by participant, admin, setup; written by admin, setup.

- **Naming:** `<client slug>-<hero|logo|background|tile>-<10 hex of the SHA-256 of the file>.<png|webp|jpg>`, flat in the library's root folder. A different picture has a different name, so an address never changes what it shows; the file a new picture replaces is moved to the recycle bin once nothing uses it.
- **What is stored:** PNG, JPEG or WebP only (never SVG), cropped and re-encoded in the browser first: hero 1200x1200 (300 KB), logo 800x400 (150 KB), background 1536x2048 (350 KB), answer tile 480x320 (60 KB); 512 KB at most.
- **Permissions:** facilitators add files and recycle them; Setup's "Seed sample clients" adds the six sample pictures; every account that opens the participant page reads them.

## Permissions

Worked out from who reads and writes each list (the `reads` and `writes` of pms-schema-meta.js, by scripts/permissions.js; the release package's RUNBOOK.md has the same table). SharePoint has no "write but not read" for a list: a page that writes a list needs Contribute there, one that only reads it needs Read, and a list it does neither with is one its accounts must not be able to read. **Participant accounts must not read PMSAdminUsers**: it holds the facilitators' PIN hashes, and the PIN only gates the admin page's screens, so the list's permission is the real lock. A facilitator who also opens the participant page needs the participant accounts' rights as well.

| List | What it holds | Participant accounts (the iPads) | Facilitators (admin.html) |
|---|---|---|---|
| PMSClients | One item for each client: its name, its slug and its look. | Read | Contribute (add and edit items) |
| PMSClientSessions | One item for each client and day: the session participants join when it is live. | Contribute (add and edit items) | Contribute (add and edit items) |
| PMSActivities | The activities: each belongs to one client and holds its questions in order. | Read | Contribute (add and edit items) |
| PMSActivityQuestions | The questions of every activity. | Read | Contribute (add and edit items) |
| PMSAnswerOptions | The answers a question offers, including which one is right. | Read | Contribute (add and edit items) |
| PMSParticipants | One item for each visit: one person on one device in one session. | Contribute (add and edit items) | Contribute (add and edit items) |
| PMSGuestQRCodes | One item for each single-use QR code. | Contribute (add and edit items) | Contribute (add and edit items) |
| PMSAppSettings | One item, `default`: which session and client are live, and the version of the lists. Every page reads it first. Setup writes it when it makes the lists; nobody makes it by hand. | Read | Contribute (add and edit items) |
| PMSGuestList | The guest list: one item for each named guest of a session. | Read | Contribute (add and edit items) |
| PMSVisitLog | The visit log: one row for each browser tab that opened the participant page. Results read it for names. | Contribute (add and edit items) | Read |
| PMSAdminUsers | The facilitators who may unlock the admin page: a name and a hash of a PIN each. | **No access** | Read |
| PMSParticipantAnswers | The answers: one item for each visit, holding all of that person's answers. | Contribute (add and edit items) | Contribute (add and edit items) |
| PMSClientImages | The clients' pictures (hero badge, logo, background, answer tiles), each stored once under a name made from its content. | Read | Contribute (add and recycle files) |

Setup is run by a site owner (Full Control of the site): it creates the lists and the library, reads every list's columns, writes the version item, adds the admins and uploads the sample pictures.

## How to change a list

**To add a column:**

1. Add the field to its list in `public/js/pms-schema.js`: the record's property, the column's internal name, its kind (text, `number`, `yesno`, `date`, `array`, `object`), and `indexed` if the app will filter on it.
2. Describe the column in `public/js/pms-schema-meta.js`, in the same place among its list's columns: its SharePoint type, its purpose in one sentence, and whatever applies of allowed values, longest value, default, who reads and writes it and whether it holds personal data.
3. Write the code that uses the field (the data layer reads and writes every field of the schema by itself).
4. Run `npm run build:lists-reference` and commit this file with the change. `npm test` (scripts/test-schema.js) fails if the two schema files disagree, and scripts/test-lists-reference.js if this file is stale.
5. If lists already exist on a site, Setup adds the column there: **Show the plan** names it and **Create** makes it (or make it by hand, exactly as this file says). If the change is one an older build cannot work with, raise `VERSION` in pms-schema.js: on a site of the earlier version the pages then stop with PMS-LST-011 until Setup has run Show the plan, Create and Mark the site as ready, which raises the version once the check is clean (Phase 10i).

**To add a list:** one entry, under a new key, in each of the two schema files (its title and fields; its purpose, readers, writers, growth and columns), the data layer's functions for it, a file of the same name under `server/data/` for the local server, then as above. The settings (`"lists"`) and the mocked SharePoint take a new key by themselves.
